errors: Gauss himself flags a 'wirklicher Rechnungsfehler' in the final digits of log ϖ. The first total 0.11761 22245 79919 93424 is corrected to …94762 and then to …94586 18851 58564. The source of the error cannot be pinned down from the visible pieces, which (as far as checked) agree with the true values of log 339, log 225 and log 1.000013.
The struck-out line 0.11762 34294 77122 53255 is a sign slip: log 1.000013 was added instead of subtracted. Gauss struck it out himself.

The 21st-25th decimals of log√π as transcribed ('…92717 56368') appear to differ from the true value (…92717 56341…). This may be a transcription misreading or a small slip far beyond the precision used. The 20-place results (e.g. log Π(1/4)) check out.

results.what: High-precision log10 of the lemniscatic quarter-period ϖ/2 = ∫_0^1 dt/√(1−t^4), via factorisation by 76275·1.000013 and log(1+x) ≈ M(x − x²/2).
results.modern_name: Lemniscate constant / complete elliptic integral K(1/√2)/√2; logarithm by factor reduction
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (lemniscate constant, 1798-99); Stirling computed ϖ numerically earlier

results.modern_name: Evaluation of Γ(1/4) via the lemniscate constant (Chowla–Selberg special case)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss / Legendre (Euler for the beta-integral relation)

results.what: Π(−1/4) from the reflection formula Π(z)Π(−z) = πz/sin πz.
results.modern_name: Euler reflection formula Γ(z)Γ(1−z) = π/sin πz

results.what: Table of log10 Γ(z+1) to about 20 decimals for z = n ± 1/4 via the recurrence Π(z+1) = (z+1)Π(z).
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss 1812 (Disquisitiones generales circa seriem infinitam, tables of log Π); Legendre's tables

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine high-precision computations supporting Gauss's known log-Π tables. The Γ(1/4)–lemniscate relation and the reflection formula are well known as Gauss's, or older. The only novelty is the archival detail of how the digits were obtained, including a self-flagged arithmetic error.
transcription_corrections: First line should read 1311028777146059 87 (ϖ/2 = 1.31102877714605987); the transcription has a doubled 7.
The '[-0,75-]' label beside 0.13096… is struck out. The number is log(Π(−¼)/Π(¼)), not log 0.75.
'76275' at the top is the multiplier 339·225 (×10^-5) used in the reduction.
